canonical_lore: Also known as Okuninushi, the kami who pacified and built the land of Izumo before ceding it to the heavenly deities. (Kojiki / Nihon Shoki)

domain: Storms, sea, and the slaying of Yamata-no-Orochi
canonical_lore: Born from Izanagi's nose and banished from Takamagahara, Susanoo slew the eight-headed serpent Yamata-no-Orochi and recovered the sword Kusanagi. (Kojiki / Nihon Shoki)
The maiden rescued by Susanoo from Yamata-no-Orochi and taken as his wife.

title: Heian-era scholar and statesman (845–903), deified as Tenjin
canonical_lore: A renowned poet and minister of the Heian court, later venerated nationwide as the kami of academics.
The grain spirit at the heart of the Inari cult, a child of Susanoo in the Kojiki, worshipped for the fertility of the fields and the increase of wealth.
A descendant of Susanoo who, with Sukunabikona, pacified and developed the land of Izumo before ceding it to the heavenly deities. (Kojiki / Nihon Shoki)

domain: Imperial rule and the modernization of Japan
title: 122nd Emperor of Japan (1852–1912)
canonical_lore: The emperor under whom Japan transformed from a feudal society into a modern state during the Meiji Restoration.

title: Empress consort of Emperor Meiji (1849–1914)
canonical_lore: Remembered for her patronage of women's education and of the Red Cross in Japan.
